messages:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] High 5xx rate detected on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 (incident INC-20251012-01). Auto-failover triggered; paging oncall. Please respond in-channel with blameless updates.

Alex M: oncall here, looking. Logs show a handful of GPU worker OOMs plus a subsequent backpressure spike in the router. Kicking off a fallback to the compat model (v1.2-lean) and reducing batch sizes.

Samira K: heads-up, tagging billing/support for SLA-credit triage: if we have >5 minutes of degraded service for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity, they could be eligible. @Billing Ops can you monitor?

Luca R: can someone draft a short status-page blurb? Keep it factual and non-technical. I can edit for tone.

Marie H: I'll start a customer-hold template for affected tenants. Need list of impacted accounts.

Alex M: mitigation in progress: rolled compat fallback and scaled down batch size by 30%. Error rate is dropping; P95 latency improving. Still seeing a few retries from older sessions; investigating KV cache pressure.

IncidentBot: Status update: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident state changed to Degraded -> Stabilized at 1758502860.

Samira K: quick eligibility checklist so we don't duplicate effort: 1) Confirm impacted window per tenant (start/end). 2) Confirm they’re on Dedicated or have SLA-tier subscription. 3) Compute token-based impact (delta in successful tokens / baseline) or minutes of degradation. Billing then maps to credit % per contract.

Billing Ops: acknowledged. We'll need the affected-customer list + their committed throughput/commit tier + billing contact. If you can drop a CSV with columns `customer_id, email, commit_tier, affected_start, affected_end, tokens_impacted` we can begin calculations.

Marie H: dropping a quick sample CSV I pulled from the incident pipeline (redacted):

```
customer_id,email,commit_tier,affected_start,affected_end,tokens_impacted
cust_1001,ops@acme.example,dedicated-std,2025-10-12T08:24:00Z,2025-10-12T08:33:00Z,124560
cust_1019,infra@zulu.example,dedicated-prem,2025-10-12T08:27:00Z,2025-10-12T08:40:00Z,220000
cust_1022,sre@beta.example,hosted-free,2025-10-12T08:25:00Z,2025-10-12T08:35:00Z,0
```

Marie H: note: hosted-free excluded from SLA credits per policy, but we'll still include a status notification.

Luca R: draft status-page blurb for review (short, no blame):

```
We experienced a service degradation in eu-west-1 affecting text generation requests between 08:24 and 08:40 UTC. Root cause: transient resource exhaustion in a subset of GPU workers; an automated fallback reduced customer impact. We have stabilized service and are monitoring. Affected customers (Dedicated) may be eligible for billing credits; our billing team will follow up with private notices.
```

Luca R: draft customer email for affected Dedicated customers (please edit):

```
Subject: Update: Service Degradation in eu-west-1 on 2025-10-12

Hi <Customer Name>,

We want to let you know about a service degradation that affected text generation in eu-west-1 between 08:24 and 08:40 UTC on 2025-10-12. During this window some requests experienced elevated errors and latency. We rolled an automated fallback which reduced impact and restored normal service.

Our preliminary analysis indicates that customers with Dedicated commitments may be eligible for billing credits under your SLA. We're preparing a per-account impact summary and will follow up within 3 business days with the proposed credit and next steps. No action is required from you at this time.

If you have questions or need an immediate account-level briefing, reply to this message and we'll set up a call. Apologies for the disruption and thanks for your patience.

Best,
Customer Reliability / Billing Ops (Redwood Inference)
```

Samira K: wording looks good. Two tweaks: 1) change "within 3 business days" to "within 72 hours" for faster cadence, 2) add a short internal link to the incident postmortem when available.

Luca R: updated draft applied. Final approval? If approved, Marie can trigger outbound emails for the Dedicated list; Billing will compute credits and include breakdown in the follow-up.

Billing Ops: we can compute credits in parallel. ETA to provide per-account credit calculation: 48 hours after receiving the affected list with tokens_impacted. We'll flag any anomalies or accounts that fall under special enterprise terms.

Marie H: once billing gives numbers, I'll coordinate final customer email + include the credit amount and how it will appear on their invoice. Also prepping a short internal comms snippet for GTM/AMs:

```
Summary for AMs: Incident in eu-west-1 caused brief degradation on 2025-10-12 (08:24-08:40 UTC). Dedicated customers may receive prorated credits; Billing will follow up with calculations within 48 hours. Reach out to support@redwood.example for account-specific questions.
```

Alex M: follow-ups for eng: collect heap/oom traces from the affected workers, add better pre-emptive OOM detection rule to autoscaler, and revisit batch-size heuristics for heavy KV-cache workloads. I'll open a followup ticket.

Samira K: thanks team. Action items recap: Marie -> final affected list + send initial status page + hold email; Billing Ops -> compute credits once list received (48h); Luca -> publish status-page blurb + customer email template; Alex -> postmortem/eng fixes. We'll add a note to the incident doc about the SLA-credit calculation method so it's auditable. :thumbsup:

Billing Ops: received sample CSV; please DM us the full list. We'll keep this thread updated with milestones.

Marie H: DM-ing the file now and will pin the status-page draft to the incident doc.

Luca R: publishing status page now (waiting for final ack). :eyes:

IncidentBot: Note: incident debrief scheduled in 24h.

Alex M: closing loop for oncall — monitoring looks healthy. Reopen if regressions.

Samira K: closing thread for customer comms prep. Will reopen if billing needs additional details or customers escalate. :wave:"
